solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Polish with a tongue

parts.note: a gloss is a shine or polish on a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to shine something up using one's tongue, or to speak Polish with a fluent tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossa is the anatomical and zoological term for the tongue, from Greek.

clue.text: When Jools Holland is on, Rex and others will turn up

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue says the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king
et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Musicians, T. Rex among them, will appear on Jools Holland's TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Later... with Jools Holland' is a long-running BBC music show, broadcast late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic allusion: the show's title names when the host is on air, at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Most serious, to men less silly

indicators.note: silly suggests foolishly jumbled, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling men to be less silly is the gravest advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of solemn: gravest, most earnest.

clue.text: More or less stuck? That's not good

indicators.note: 'not good' says the letter for good is removed from the word

parts.note: a ship stuck on the bottom has run aground

explanation.surface: A shrug of a reply: are you stuck, more or less? That's no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck' gives AGROUND; 'not' strips G from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: approximately, as in 'about ten' or 'roughly ten'.

clue.text: Crack soldiers trapped by wrong turning in ruined city

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, as in 'have a crack at it', which is a go

indicators.note: trapped by says the soldiers sit inside the turned word
turning says the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: harm is a wrong done to someone
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Elite troops ambushed after taking a wrong turning in a devastated city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective describing the soldiers, but it is a noun: a crack at something is an attempt. 'turning' makes MRAH.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed by fire and brimstone alongside Sodom, so a city laid in ruins.

parts.note: the cross-referenced answers read as a sentence, ending 'Berlin number': a song by Irving Berlin, the composer

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the eight answers named and they read 'Bled criminal inside fine single around Berlin number'; the last two words point to Irving Berlin's patriotic song.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote this patriotic American anthem in 1918, later popularised by Kate Smith.

clue.text: Cake damage — one has fly on it

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the speeding word above the word for one

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
to zip is to fly along at speed
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A spoiled cake that has a fly sitting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect but is a verb giving ZIP; 'one' gives AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Almond paste is sold in blocks or cakes and also coats rich fruit cakes.

clue.text: A puzzle to tackle on public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: re means concerning, a subject to tackle or deal with
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: Someone with a crossword to tackle on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a word puzzle made of pictures and letters.

clue.text: Narrative can lead to novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A storyteller notes that a narrative can grow into a full-length novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book that a narrative leads to, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Based on stories and personal accounts rather than facts, as in narrative evidence.

clue.text: Under any circumstances class is tough

definitions.note: the adjective stands for a noun phrase used after 'is': saying a task is tough is saying it is a demanding request

parts.note: 'not at all' means not under any circumstances
an order is a class or rank, as in the lower orders

explanation.surface: A teacher's complaint that, whatever happens, this class is a hard one.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun phrase, so the swap works in the clue's own frame: 'class is tough' reads as the thing being a hard demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a task or request that is very difficult to fulfil.

clue.text: Run like Bannister, Budd, Bolt?

definitions.meaning: colours run when the dye spreads, past tense
each surname begins with the letter B, so each is led by B

explanation.surface: A puzzle about running in the style of three famous athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Bannister, Zola Budd and Usain Bolt were runners, so 'Run' looks like a link to them; the second reading splits the answer as B-LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dye that has spread out of place has seeped, and three names starting with B are headed by that letter.

clue.text: Lawless US state keeping border lit

indicators.note: keeping says the state's letters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
a rim is an edge or border
a fire that is lit is still in

explanation.surface: A lawless American state keeping its frontier lit up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit' gives IN, as a fire that is still burning is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting against the law means being outside the law.

clue.text: Middle of bed is nicely turned

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
of says the letters are taken from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The centre of the bed has been neatly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the letters as part of the words that follow; 'turned' reads EDISNI back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the middle of something is its interior or central part.

clue.text: Clear penalty

definitions.meaning: weather that is clear is bright and dry
a sum of money paid as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Clear skies make for good weather, and a monetary punishment is a standard sense.

clue.text: What's thought of old nursing home I'm heading

indicators.note: heading places the contraction at the top of the down answer
nursing says the word for old holds the word for home

parts.note: ageing, or aging, means growing old
being in is being at home

explanation.surface: An old nursing home matron's thought about where she is going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing home' reads as one institution, but 'nursing' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: something conceived by the mind, a fancy or idea.

clue.text: Disconnected, as censor after rejected musical

indicators.note: after places the censor's name behind the turned title
rejected means sent back, so the show's title is read backwards

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
Cato the Elder was the famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: A disjointed review, as a critic judges a musical he has rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'censor' is Cato, a Roman magistrate who held that office; 'rejected' turns CATS to STAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term for notes played short and detached from each other.

clue.text: Sister hugged by kid with drink problem

indicators.note: with joins the drink on after the rest
hugged by says the sister is enclosed in the word for kid

parts.note: to cod is to hoax or kid someone
a nun is a religious sister
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A nun clasped by a child who has a drinking problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but is the verb meaning to tease, COD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a puzzling question or difficult problem.

clue.text: Gloat about guards before getting intimate

indicators.note: guards says the shuffled letters surround the next piece
about signals the letters of the word are moved around

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone who gloats over the guards before getting close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' looks like a verb but is a noun, a close friend; 'about' gives ALTGO, and 'guards' has it surround the archaic word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun: an alter ego is a very close and trusted friend, a second self.

clue.text: Crew heading to a cape

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
till means up to, as far as

explanation.surface: A ship's crew steering for a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a headland the crew is sailing to, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace scarf or light shawl worn over the head and shoulders, a kind of short cloak.

clue.text: River duck's first to escape

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, nil

indicators.note: first to says only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A duck on a river is the first to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.

clue.text: City that's popular after live rugby

indicators.note: after places the word for popular behind the other two

parts.note: to be is to live, exist
RL is Rugby League
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A city that has taken to watching rugby live.
explanation.walkthrough: RL, Rugby League, is one of the two codes of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany.

clue.text: 45 and unmarried

definitions.meaning: a seven-inch record played at 45 rpm, holding one track a side

explanation.definitionFit: A 45 rpm record is a one-song release, and someone without a spouse is not married.

clue.text: Man's unfulfilled with two guiding spirits

indicators.note: unfulfilled says the word is left incomplete, its final letter gone

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man feels unfulfilled with two spirit guides looking after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of genius in its sense of a guardian or tutelary spirit.

clue.text: Nude painter frames queen, reflected in immortality

indicators.note: frames says the painter's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter famous for his nudes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: reflected says the little word is mirrored, read backwards

explanation.surface: A painter of nudes portrays the queen, captured for ever in his art.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty (1787-1849) was notorious in Victorian Britain for his nudes; 'reflected' makes NI, and 'frames' wraps the painter round both small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: endless existence, living forever.

clue.text: Peg in a sort of square opening

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing instrument
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A square peg in a round hole, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'a square peg in a round hole'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thole is a pin set in a boat's gunwale as a rowlock for an oar.

clue.text: Place for firing line — one's own houses

indicators.note: houses says the family word holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: one's own people are one's family, kin

explanation.surface: A firing line where every man protects his own family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests guns, but it is firing pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven in which pottery and bricks are baked hard.

clue.text: When empty, eat sandwiches or boiled fresh carrot?

indicators.note: sandwiches says the remaining letters enclose the rearranged ones
emptied of its middle, only the outside letters of the word remain
fresh means made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook's question about whether to eat a carrot in sandwiches, boiled or raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the container signal; 'fresh' makes DIBLEROO. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an example of a vegetable whose underground part we eat.

clue.text: Recalled song about officer following a grand Roman general

indicators.note: following says the turned song comes after the first two letters

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: about says the reversed song goes round the officer
recalled means called back, so the song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a song about an officer who served under a great Roman commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' looks like remembering but means sent back, making RIA; 'about' sets it round the officer, after A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius Agricola was the Roman governor and military commander famed for campaigns in Britain.

clue.text: Figure close to John Brown

indicators.note: close to means the end of the name, its final letter

parts.note: umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A notable figure close to a man named John Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Brown' looks like one person's name; 'Brown' is the pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a figure is a numeral, a digit.
